nav.intent: First-class daemon-owned watchdogs for pij sessions: universal 20-min default, self-teaching pause/resume turns, compact auto-pause, blind-fire through usage-limit freezes with deterministic unresponsive/stalled detection, cost-bounded on-fire tmux pane-text capture

nodes.label: Research
instructions: Explore how the relevant code works before you plan — start cheap, climb only when the evidence demands it; never jump straight to a plan.
Run /builder 1a explore "<intent>" — it produces research-dossier.md, a decision packet (not a transcript) with evidence links.
Done when the dossier names the core decision the plan must resolve and the findings that bound it.
nodes.note: Deep lead-only dossier: 11 findings, 6 historical; freeze invisible by design (working-gated staleness + transient-quota→unknown); PeerWatchManager = template; capture cost = context injection, not tmux capture

nodes.label: Plan
instructions: Write ONE planning document in a single atomic pass — `## Business Specification` (WHAT/WHY) on top, `## Implementation Plan` (HOW: phases, task tables, acceptance criteria, gates G1–G7) below.
Run /builder 1b plan "<intent>" (add --simple for a one-phase flow); it front-loads the clarifying questions, then auto-runs /validate-v2.
Done when <slug>-plan.md carries both halves and reads **Status**: READY — DRAFT means a gate FAILed, so resolve the gaps and re-run.

nodes.label: Ship
instructions: Get the work out — push the branch, open a PR (using the repo's PR guidance), watch its CI checks, and report problems; the merge itself is optional.
Run /builder 8 ship --plan "<plan path>"; push and PR-open each pause for a separate confirm, and any merge waits for a typed PROCEED.
Done when the PR is open and its checks are green (or the failures are reported with a fix-loop offer); a diverged base hands off to 8c reconcile.

nodes.label: Backpressure survey
instructions: Pre-coding seam: survey what the harness can PROVE about the plan's coverage versus what was only eyeballed, then re-plan informed by it.
Run /eng-harness-flow --hook pre-coding --json — a REAL invocation, never narrated; the plan verb does not auto-read the coverage, so fold the findings in yourself.

On done, receipt first, status second: harness flow comment --path <flow-path> --node backpressure --kind validation --source agent --text "decision:<…> verdict:<…> time:<…> basis_sha256:<full SHA-256 of the plan file>" THEN harness flow status --path <flow-path> --node backpressure --to done. Mandatory unless the human declines — a decline is: harness flow comment --path <flow-path> --node backpressure --kind decision --source user --text "<their verbatim words>" THEN harness flow status --path <flow-path> --node backpressure --to skipped; never a narrated skip.

Basis is the LATEST plan: on each guided entry recompute the plan file's SHA-256 — a mismatch with (or absence of) the recorded basis_sha256 re-opens this seam via a deterministic new chore, id backpressure-<first 12 hex of that SHA-256> (full hash in its receipt; same bytes re-use this node + receipt, changed bytes create exactly one new node; never resurrect this one — D5).

Router missing, or envelope noop/UNAVAILABLE → same two calls with the detection receipt/envelope as the text: harness flow comment --path <flow-path> --node backpressure --kind validation --source agent --text "decision:unavailable reason:<…> time:<…>" THEN harness flow status --path <flow-path> --node backpressure --to done — a completed attempt, not a skip.
